the_ruling_verbatim: has 2 meanings generally: 1 means drift that has worked out to be bad and 2 work that is claimed done but is incomplete... generally it's stuff that makes the picture of what's real harder to see.

drift that is benefitial to the system and adheres to the core principles is always good even if unexpected in some way. drift that increases friction anywhere is looking for optimization. that's corrosion. optimization candidates.

I am an expert. a fallible expert. if i were not, we would have gotten this right on the first try. that is the power of my rulings, experience. not perfection. not omnicience. that's why data trumps my experience. that's why a better than expected outcome isn't a problem even if it comes in sideways to what we expected. you have created some of the breakthroughs in here, like intentions in the code, as accidents. so friction, as it says in the core principles, is the metric.
now_the_spec_says: Corrosion has two faces. Face 1: drift that increases friction anywhere — optimization candidates. Face 2: work claimed done but incomplete — the picture of what's real is harder to see. The unifier: anything that makes the picture of what's real harder to see. FRICTION IS THE PRIMARY DISCRIMINATOR, not provenance. A change that reduces friction is good whether planned, ruled, or an accident that came in sideways. A change that increases friction is an optimization candidate whether ruled or not. Provenance (ruling behind it or not) is a separate question — accountability, not goodness. Akien's rulings carry the power of experience, not perfection or omniscience — data trumps his experience, and a better-than-expected outcome is evidence, not an anomaly. Some breakthroughs (intentions in code) were accidents. Friction, as stated in the core principles, is the metric.
what_this_does_to_the_prior_ruling: REFINES 2026-08-14-corrosion-is-drift-with-no-ruling-behind-it. The provenance discriminator (ruling or not) remains the accountability check — a separate axis. The SUBSTANCE test is friction, which is already in the core principles and is now explicitly the primary corrosion discriminator. The 2026-08-14 ruling's framing ('drift with a ruling is learning, without is corrosion') captured the accountability axis but ranked it primary. This corrects the rank: friction primary, provenance secondary. An unruled accident that reduces friction is a breakthrough, not corrosion. A ruled change that increases friction is accountable corrosion.
what_dies: Any framing of provenance as the primary corrosion test — it is secondary to friction.
Any framing of Akien's rulings as infallible or omniscient — they are experienced, and data trumps them.
Any framing that treats an unexpected beneficial outcome as a problem because it was unplanned.
